tier_rationale: Manufacturer product documentation lists a 10-minute dial timer with four power levels and no connectivity, programmable memory or app feature; the sibling RCS10TS in the same series is the touch-control programmable variant, confirming the dial model is a deliberate tier.
the_unplug_test: You turn a dial. It runs for that long and stops. There is nothing to set up, nothing to pair, no clock that flashes after a power cut, and no company involved in heating your food. If you open the door mid-cycle the timer resets to zero, which is the entire complexity budget of this appliance.

repairability.notes: Commercial food-service equipment: rated 100 cycles/day, parts distributed through restaurant supply channels, and designed to be repaired rather than replaced. Stainless interior and exterior.

sources.supports: Manufacturer (ACP Inc, who make Amana Commercial microwaves) documents the RCS10DSE as the dial-control model: 10-minute timer auto-resetting to zero, 4 power levels, 1000 W, 1.2 cu ft, 100 cycles/day. No WiFi, programmable memory or app feature listed. Sibling control: the RCS10TS in the same series is the touch-control model with 100 programmable menu items.
Distributor listing corroborating current availability at $487 and describing mechanical dial controls with no digital or connected features.

open_questions: Consumer microwaves are a harder problem than this commercial one — worth a separate pass to find a domestic model with mechanical controls still in production.
notes: Another instance of the commercial-grade escape hatch. It costs more than a domestic microwave and is plainly better built, and its simplicity is a commercial requirement rather than a nostalgia feature: a kitchen cannot have staff learning a menu system.
